title.zh: 卷一百八十七 列傳第七十四: 烏古孫良楨 賈魯 逯魯曾 貢師泰 周伯琦 吳當
title.en: Volume 187 Biographies 74: Wugusunliangzhen, Jia Lu, Lu Luceng, Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, Wu Dang
title.raw: 卷一百八十七 列傳第七十四: 烏古孫良楨 賈魯 逯魯曾 貢師泰 周伯琦 吳當 Volume 187 Biographies 74: Wugusunliangzhen, Jia Lu, Lu Luceng, Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, Wu Dang

sentences.zh: 烏古孫良楨

translations.literal: Wugusun Liangzhen
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Liangzhen

sentences.zh: 烏古孫良楨字幹卿，世次見父澤傳。

translations.literal: Wugusun Liangzhen, courtesy name Ganqing; his place in the lineage is given in the biography of his father Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Wugusun Liangzhen, styled Ganqing, is listed in the genealogical sequence in his father Ze's biography.

sentences.zh: 資器絕人，好讀書。

translations.literal: His natural endowment surpassed other men, and he loved to read books.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed exceptional talent and was devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，蔭補江陰州判官，尋丁內艱，服除，調婺州武義縣尹，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he received a yin appointment as assistant prefect of Jiangyin Prefecture; soon after he entered mourning for his mother, and when the mourning period ended he was transferred to be magistrate of Wuyi County in Wuzhou, where he carried out benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1322 he entered office through hereditary privilege as assistant prefect of Jiangyin; shortly afterward his mother died and he withdrew for mourning. After the mourning period he was assigned magistrate of Wuyi in Wuzhou, where his policies brought real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 改漳州路推官，獄有疑者，悉平反之。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as judicial investigator of Zhangzhou Circuit; in cases where imprisonment raised doubts, he reversed all of them.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of judicial investigator in Zhangzhou Circuit, and every doubtful case in the prisons he set right.

sentences.zh: 上言：「律，徒者不杖，今杖而又徒，非恤刑意，宜加徒減杖。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "According to the statutes, those sentenced to penal servitude are not to be caned; now they are caned and also sentenced to servitude—this is not in the spirit of merciful punishment. Servitude should be increased and caning reduced."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "The code provides that convicts sentenced to penal servitude shall not also be flogged, yet now flogging is combined with servitude. That contradicts the intent of lenient punishment; the penalty of servitude should be increased in place of reducing the strokes of the rod."

sentences.zh: 」遂定為令。

translations.literal: This was thereupon fixed as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 移泉州，益以能稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Quanzhou and came to be still more renowned for his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Quanzhou, he grew still more celebrated for his ability.

sentences.zh: 轉延平判官，拜陝西行臺監察御史，劾遼陽行省左丞相達識帖睦邇賣國不忠，援漢高帝斬丁公故事，以明人臣大義。

translations.literal: He became an assistant of Yanping, was appointed Surveillance Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and impeached Toghuz Temür, Left Chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for selling out the state and disloyalty, citing the Han Gaozu precedent of executing Duke Ding to clarify the great duty of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to assistant official of Yanping, he was appointed surveillance censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and impeached Toghuz Temür, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the realm, invoking Emperor Gaozu of Han's execution of Duke Ding to illustrate a minister's paramount obligation.

sentences.zh: 并劾御史中丞胡居祐奸邪，皆罷之，中外震懾。

translations.literal: He also impeached the Censor-in-Chief Hu Juyou for wickedness; both were dismissed, and court and countryside were shaken with awe.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Censor-in-Chief Hu Juyou as corrupt and treacherous; both men were removed from office, and the whole empire was awestruck.

sentences.zh: 陞都事，猶以言不盡行，解去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretariat supervisor, but because his words were not fully carried out, he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to secretariat supervisor, he resigned when he saw his recommendations were not being implemented in full.

sentences.zh: 復起為監察御史，良楨以帝方覽萬幾，不可不求賢自輔，於是連疏：「天曆數年間紀綱大壞，元氣傷夷。

translations.literal: He was recalled as a surveillance censor. Liangzhen, considering that the emperor had just taken up the myriad affairs of state and could not fail to seek worthies to assist him, submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianshun years the laws and ordinances were greatly ruined and the vital energy of the realm was injured and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as surveillance censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now attending to every matter of government, he must seek worthy men to aid him. He therefore submitted memorial after memorial: "In the Tianshun period the institutions of state were gravely corrupted and the political order grievously depleted.

sentences.zh: 天祐聖明，入膺大統，而西宮秉政，奸臣弄權，畜憾十有餘年。

translations.literal: Heaven blessed his sagacity and enlightenment; he inherited the great succession, yet the Western Palace held power and treacherous ministers manipulated authority, nursing resentment for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blessed Your Sagely Enlightenment when you ascended the great succession, yet the western palace faction held power and corrupt ministers manipulated authority, harboring resentments for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 天威一怒，陰晦開明，以正大名，以章大孝，此誠兢兢業業祈天永命之秋，其術在乎敬身修德而已。

translations.literal: When Heaven's majesty was aroused once in anger, obscurity was opened into brightness, the great title was rectified, and great filial piety was displayed—this is truly the season for trembling care in praying Heaven for enduring mandate; the method lies only in revering the person and cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's wrath flared once, darkness gave way to light: the great succession was set right and supreme filial duty was proclaimed. This is precisely the moment to serve Heaven with reverent care and pray for a lasting mandate—the means lie solely in cultivating the self and perfecting virtue.

sentences.zh: 今經筵多領以職事臣，數日一進講，不渝數刻已罷，而御小臣，恒侍左右，何益於盛德哉。

translations.literal: Now the classics lecture is mostly headed by officials burdened with duties; they lecture once every several days and dismiss it within no more than a few moments, while favored petty attendants constantly wait at left and right—what benefit is this to magnificent virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Today the lecture to the throne is largely entrusted to officials already burdened with office; they lecture only every few days and finish within a few moments, while favored attendants remain constantly at Your side. What profit does this bring to the cultivation of supreme virtue?

sentences.zh: 臣願招延儒臣若許衡者數人，置於禁密，常以唐、虞、三代之道，啟沃宸衷，日新其德，實萬世無疆之福也。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to summon and retain several Confucian ministers such as Xu Heng, place them within the forbidden precincts, and constantly use the Way of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties to enrich the imperial heart, renewing his virtue daily—this would truly be a blessing without boundary for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that several scholar-officials of Xu Heng's caliber be invited to reside within the inner palace, there to nourish Your Majesty's mind unceasingly with the traditions of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, day by day renewing Your virtue—a blessing without limit for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 」又以國俗父死則妻其從母，兄弟死則收其妻，父母死無憂制，遂言：「綱常皆出於天而不可變，議法之吏，乃言國人不拘此例，諸國人各從本俗。

translations.literal: " He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his father's younger brother's wife, and when a brother dies one takes his wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance. He therefore stated: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed, yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.
translations.idiomatic: " He also addressed the national custom whereby a man marries his stepmother after his father's death and takes his brother's widow after a brother's death, with no mourning prescribed when parents die. He argued: "The bonds of human relations derive from Heaven and are immutable, yet the officials who draft law claim that Mongols need not observe these norms and that subjects of the various states may each follow their native customs.

sentences.zh: 是漢、南人當守綱常，國人、諸國人不必守綱常也。

translations.literal: Thus Han Chinese and southerners must uphold the constants, while Mongols and people of the various states need not uphold the constants.
translations.idiomatic: In effect this means that Han Chinese and southerners must uphold moral order, while Mongols and other subject peoples need not.

sentences.zh: 名曰優之，實則陷之，外若尊之，內實侮之，推其本心所以待國人者，不若漢、南人之厚也。

translations.literal: It is called favoring them, but in reality it traps them; outwardly they seem to be honored, but inwardly they are truly insulted. Inferring the true heart with which Mongols are treated, it is not as generous as toward Han Chinese and southerners.
translations.idiomatic: What is called granting them privilege in fact ensnares them; outwardly they seem honored, yet inwardly they are despised. Judging by the government's true attitude, Mongols are treated less generously than Han Chinese and southerners.

sentences.zh: 請下禮官有司及右科進士在朝者會議，自天子至於庶人，皆從禮制，以成列聖未遑之典，明萬世不易之道。

translations.literal: He requested that the ritual officials, the relevant offices, and jinshi of the Right Branch in court confer, so that from the Son of Heaven down to the common people all would follow ritual regulations, thereby completing the canon that successive sages had not yet had leisure to establish and clarifying the Way unchanging for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that ritual officials, the relevant departments, and Right Branch jinshi at court deliberate together so that from the Son of Heaven to the common people all would follow the ritual code—thus fulfilling the canon successive sage emperors had not yet completed and affirming the eternal Way.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「隱士劉因，道學經術可比許文正公衡，從祀孔子廟庭。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The recluse Liu Yin, in the learning of the Way and in classical studies, may be compared to Duke of Culture Xu Heng; let him be granted secondary sacrifice in the Confucian temple."
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged that the recluse Liu Yin, whose mastery of the Way and classical learning rivaled that of Xu Heng, Duke of Culture, be granted secondary sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: " None received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals received a reply.

sentences.zh: 御史臺作新風憲，復疏其所當行者，以舉賢才為綱，而以厚風俗、均賦役、重審理、汰冗官、選守令、出奉使、均公田為目，指擿剴切，雖觸忌諱，亦不顧也。

translations.literal: When the Censorate drew up new surveillance statutes, he again memorialized what ought to be carried out, taking the elevation of worthy talent as the main theme and, as headings, enriching customs, equalizing taxes and corvée, emphasizing judicial review, eliminating superfluous officials, selecting prefects and magistrates, dispatching imperial envoys, and equalizing public fields; his criticisms were incisive, and even when they touched taboos he did not care.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate promulgated new surveillance regulations, he submitted another detailed memorial on what should be done: promoting worthy talent as the overarching principle, with enriching customs, equalizing taxes and labor service, strengthening judicial review, eliminating redundant officials, selecting prefects and magistrates, dispatching imperial envoys, and equalizing public fields as specific measures. His criticisms were sharp and forthright; even when they touched forbidden topics he did not hold back.

sentences.zh: 宦者罕失嬖妾殺其妻，糜其肉飼犬，上疏乞正重刑，并論宦寺結廷臣撓政為害，可汰黜之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Han Shi, having lost a favored concubine, killed his wife, ground her flesh, and fed it to dogs. He submitted a memorial requesting severe punishment, and also argued that eunuchs banding with court ministers to obstruct government was harmful and that they could be eliminated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Han Shi killed his wife, ground her flesh, and fed it to his dogs after losing a favored concubine, Liangzhen memorialized for severe punishment. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government should be purged.

sentences.zh: 憸佞側目。

translations.literal: The sycophantic and servile glared at him sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: The sycophants and flatterers glared at him with hatred.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，召為刑部員外郎，轉御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Punishments and transferred to be secretariat supervisor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1344 he was summoned as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and then transferred to secretariat supervisor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 五年，改中書左司都事，出為江東道肅政廉訪司副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to secretariat supervisor of the Left Secretariat Department and went out as Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reassigned as secretariat supervisor of the Left Secretariat Department and appointed deputy surveillance commissioner of the Jiangdong Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 上官一日，辭歸。

translations.literal: After one day in office he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a single day in the post he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 六年，授平江路緫管，不拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed general manager of Pingjiang Circuit but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In 1346 he was offered the post of general manager of Pingjiang Circuit but declined it.

sentences.zh: 八年，復召為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again summoned as Vice Minister of the Right Secretariat Department.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he was recalled as vice minister of the Right Secretariat Department.

sentences.zh: 九年，陞郎中，尋遷廣東道肅政廉訪使，未行，還為郎中，遷福建道肅政廉訪使，中道召還，參議中書省事，兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to director; soon after he was transferred to be Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong Circuit, but before departing he was returned to director, then transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian Circuit; mid-journey he was recalled and made Associate Administrator of Secretariat Affairs, concurrently a classics-lecture official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1349 he was promoted to director. He was soon appointed surveillance commissioner of Guangdong but before taking up the post was returned to his former rank as director, then appointed surveillance commissioner of Fujian. Recalled en route, he became associate administrator of Secretariat affairs and concurrently a lecturer at the classics lecture to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜治書侍御史，陞中書參知政事、同知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Attending Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Associate Administrator of the Secretariat and Concurrent Administrator of the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 he was appointed attending censor-in-chief and promoted to associate administrator of the Secretariat and concurrent administrator of the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年，陞左丞，兼大司農卿，仍同知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Left Chancellor, concurrently Minister of the Grand Agrarian Office, and still Concurrent Administrator of the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353 he was promoted to left chancellor, concurrently minister of the Grand Agrarian Office, while retaining his post as concurrent administrator of the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 時中書參用非人，事多異同，不得一一如志。

translations.literal: At that time the Secretariat employed unworthy men; affairs often differed and conflicted, and he could not carry out his will in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Secretariat was staffed with unworthy men; policies often diverged and conflicted, and he could not always carry out his intentions.

sentences.zh: 會軍餉不給，請與右丞悟良哈台主屯田，歲入二十萬石。

translations.literal: When military provisions were insufficient, he requested to take charge of garrison farming together with Right Chancellor Ulabuqatai, with an annual yield of two hundred thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When military provisions ran short, he asked to oversee garrison farming jointly with Right Chancellor Ulabuqatai, producing two hundred thousand piculs per year.

sentences.zh: 東宮久未建，懇懇為言，車駕幸上都，始冊皇太子。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace had long gone unestablished; he pleaded earnestly on the matter, and when the imperial carriage visited Shangdu, the crown prince was at last enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had long gone uninstalled; Liangzhen pleaded earnestly on the matter, and when the emperor traveled to Shangdu the crown prince was at last formally installed.

sentences.zh: 立詹事院，驛召為副詹事，每直端本堂，則進正心誠意之說、親君子遠小人之道，皇太子嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was established, he was summoned by post as Vice Household Master; whenever he attended at the Hall of the Correct Root, he advanced the doctrine of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere and the Way of drawing near to gentlemen and keeping distant from petty men, and the crown prince praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Household of the Heir Apparent was established, he was summoned by express post as vice household master. Whenever he attended at the Hall of the Correct Root he expounded the doctrine of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere and the principle of drawing near to gentlemen while keeping petty men at a distance; the crown prince welcomed his teaching.

sentences.zh: 當時盜賊蜂起，帝聞，惡之，下詔分討，必盡誅而後已。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels swarmed forth; when the emperor heard of it he detested them and issued an edict for separate suppression, declaring that they must all be exterminated before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and rebels were rising everywhere; when the emperor heard of it he was filled with loathing and issued an edict for their suppression on every front, vowing that none would be spared until all were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 良楨言：「平賊在收人心，以回天意，多殺非道也。

translations.literal: Liangzhen said: "Pacifying rebels lies in winning people's hearts and turning back Heaven's intent; excessive killing is not the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhen argued: "To pacify rebels one must win the people's hearts and turn Heaven's mind back to favor; indiscriminate slaughter is not the Way."

sentences.zh: 」乃赦以安之。

translations.literal: An amnesty was thereupon issued to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was issued to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷淮南行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to be Left Chancellor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he was transferred to left chancellor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，泰州賊張士誠既降復叛，殺淮南行省參知政事趙璉，進據高郵、六合，太師脫脫奉詔，緫諸王軍南征，而良楨洎參議龔伯璲、刑部主事廬山等從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Taizhou rebel Zhang Shicheng had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Zhao Lian, Associate Administrator of the Huainan Branch Secretariat; he advanced to occupy Gaoyou and Liuhe. Grand Preceptor Toghto received the edict and commanded the armies of the princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen together with Associate Administrator Gong Bojiong, Registrar of the Ministry of Punishments Lu Shan, and others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Taizhou rebel Zhang Shicheng had surrendered and then rebelled again, killing Zhao Lian, associate administrator of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, and seizing Gaoyou and Liuhe. Grand Preceptor Toghto received orders to command the princes' armies on a southern campaign, accompanied by Liangzhen, Associate Administrator Gong Bojiong, Ministry of Punishments registrar Lu Shan, and others.

sentences.zh: 既平六合，垂克高郵，會詔罷脫脫兵柄，遂有上變告伯璲等勸脫脫勒兵北向者，下其事逮問，詞連良楨，簿對無所驗。

translations.literal: After Liuhe was pacified and Gaoyou was on the verge of capture, an edict arrived stripping Toghto of military authority; thereupon someone submitted a report of irregularity accusing Gong Bojiong and others of urging Toghto to force the army northward. The matter was sent down for arrest and interrogation; the testimony implicated Liangzhen, but examination of the records found nothing verified.
translations.idiomatic: After Liuhe was pacified and Gaoyou was nearly taken, an edict arrived stripping Toghto of military command. Someone then denounced Gong Bojiong and others for urging Toghto to march the army northward. The case was sent down for arrest and interrogation; testimony implicated Liangzhen, but examination of the records found no evidence against him.

sentences.zh: 即日還中書左丞，命分省彰德，主調軍食，居半歲，還中書。

translations.literal: That same day he was restored as Left Chancellor of the Secretariat and ordered to branch-secretariat at Zhangde to take charge of provisioning military grain; after half a year he returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was restored as left chancellor of the Secretariat and assigned to the Zhangde branch secretariat to oversee military provisions. After half a year he returned to the central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進階榮祿大夫，賜玉帶一。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced in rank to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and granted one jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356 he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and granted a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除大司農。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Minister of the Grand Agrarian Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1357 he was appointed minister of the Grand Agrarian Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，陞右丞，兼大司農，辭，不允。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Right Chancellor, concurrently Minister of the Grand Agrarian Office; he declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to right chancellor while retaining the Grand Agrarian Office; he declined but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 論罷陷賊延坐之令。

translations.literal: He argued for abolishing the ordinance on extended punishment for those implicated with rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He argued successfully for abolishing the ordinance that extended punishment to the families of those implicated with rebels.

sentences.zh: 有惡少年誣知宜興州張復通賊之罪，中書將籍其孥，吏抱案請署。

translations.literal: A vicious youth falsely accused Zhang Fu, prefect of Yixing, of communicating with rebels; the Secretariat was about to register his household for confiscation, and a clerk brought the dossier requesting signature.
translations.idiomatic: A vicious youth falsely accused Zhang Fu, prefect of Yixing, of colluding with rebels; the Secretariat was about to register his family for confiscation, and a clerk brought the dossier for signature.

sentences.zh: 良楨曰；

translations.literal: Liangzhen said:
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhen said:

sentences.zh: 「手可斷，案不可署。

translations.literal: "My hand may be cut off, but this dossier I will not sign."
translations.idiomatic: "My hand may be cut off, but I will not sign this dossier."

sentences.zh: 」同列變色，卒不署。

translations.literal: His colleagues changed color, but in the end he did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues blanched, but in the end he refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 良楨自左曹登政府，多所建白。

translations.literal: From the time Liangzhen rose from the Left Secretariat Department to enter the government, he made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Liangzhen rose from the Left Secretariat Department into high office, he offered many constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 罷福建、山東食鹽，浙東、西長生牛租，瀕海被災圍田稅，民皆德之。

translations.literal: He abolished the salt monopoly in Fujian and Shandong, the long-life ox tax in eastern and western Zhejiang, and the encircled-field tax in coastal disaster areas; the people all regarded him with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the salt monopoly in Fujian and Shandong, the long-life ox levy in eastern and western Zhejiang, and encircled-field taxes in coastal disaster zones; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 嘗論至正格輕重不倫，吏得並緣為奸，舉明律者數人，參酌古今，重定律書，書成而罷。

translations.literal: He once argued that the Zhizheng code was inconsistent in severity and leniency, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit wrongdoing; he nominated several men versed in Ming law, consulted past and present, and redrafted the code book, but when the book was completed the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that the Zhizheng code was inconsistent in the severity of penalties, enabling clerks to exploit the gaps for corruption. He nominated several experts in Ming law to consult past and present precedents and redraft the legal code; when the work was completed the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 家居輒訓諸子曰：「吾無過人者，惟待人以誠，人亦以誠遇我，汝宜志之。

translations.literal: At home he would instruct his sons, saying: "I have nothing surpassing others; only in treating people with sincerity do others also meet me with sincerity—you should keep this in mind."
translations.idiomatic: At home he often admonished his sons: "I have no special gift beyond this: treat others with sincerity, and they will meet you with sincerity. Remember that."

sentences.zh: 」晚歲病瘠，數謁告，病益侵，遂卒。

translations.literal: In his later years he grew ill and emaciated, repeatedly requested leave, his illness increasingly encroached, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew ill and wasted away; he repeatedly requested leave, his illness worsened, and he died.

sentences.zh: 自號約齋。

translations.literal: He styled himself Studio of Restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Yuezhai, Studio of Restraint.

sentences.zh: 有詩文奏議凡若干卷，藏于家。

translations.literal: He had poetry, prose, and memorials totaling several juan, kept in his household.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poetry, prose, and memorials, totaling several juan, were kept in his family.

sentences.zh: 賈魯字友恒，河東高平人。

translations.literal: Jia Lu, courtesy name Youheng, was a native of Gaoping in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lu, styled Youheng, was a native of Gaoping in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 幼負志節，既長，謀略過人。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed resolve and integrity; when grown, his stratagems surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong character; as a man his strategic judgment surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 延祐、至治間，兩以明經領鄉貢。

translations.literal: Between the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he twice led the provincial tribute selection through mastery of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he twice led the provincial tribute selection through mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，恩授東平路儒學教授，辟憲史，歷行省掾，除潞城縣尹，選丞相東曹掾，擢戶部主事，未上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he received a grace appointment as professor of the Confucian school of Dongping Circuit, was recruited as a surveillance clerk, served as a branch-secretariat clerk, was appointed magistrate of Lucheng County, was selected as a clerk in the Chancellor's Eastern Department, and was promoted to Registrar of the Ministry of Revenue, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he received a grace appointment as professor of the Confucian school in Dongping Circuit, then served as surveillance clerk and branch-secretariat clerk, was appointed magistrate of Lucheng, selected as clerk in the chancellor's Eastern Department, and promoted to registrar of the Ministry of Revenue—but before he could take up the post,

sentences.zh: 一日，覺心悸，尋得父書，筆勢顫縮，即辭歸，比至家，父已有風疾，未幾卒。

translations.literal: one day he felt palpitations of the heart; soon he received a letter from his father whose brushwork trembled and shrank, and he immediately resigned and returned; by the time he reached home his father already had a wind ailment, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: one day he felt his heart palpitate. Soon a letter arrived from his father, the handwriting trembling and uncertain; he resigned at once and hurried home, but by the time he arrived his father was already stricken with paralysis and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 魯居喪服闋，起為太醫院都事。

translations.literal: When Lu's mourning period ended he was recalled as secretariat supervisor of the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period Lu was recalled as secretariat supervisor of the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 會詔修遼、金、宋三史，召魯為宋史局官。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, Lu was summoned as an official of the Song History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was issued to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, Lu was summoned as an official of the Song History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 書成，選魯燕南山東道奉使宣撫幕官，考績居最，遷中書省檢校官。

translations.literal: When the books were completed, Lu was selected as a staff officer on the Pacification Commission of the Yanshan Shandong East Circuit; in performance evaluation he ranked first and was transferred to be Reviewing Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were completed, Lu was selected as staff officer on the Pacification Commission of the Yanshan Shandong East Circuit; his performance evaluation ranked first and he was transferred to reviewing officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上言：「十八河倉，近歲淪沒官糧百三十萬斛，其弊由富民兼并，貧民流亡，宜合先正經界，然事體重大，非處置盡善，不可輕發。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "At the Eighteen River granaries, in recent years one million three hundred thousand piculs of official grain have been lost to inundation; the abuse arises from rich households' encroachment and merger and the poor people's flight and exile. The boundaries should first be rectified in accordance with precedent, yet the matter is weighty in body and cannot lightly be launched unless the disposition is thoroughly sound."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "At the Eighteen River granaries, in recent years 1.3 million piculs of official grain have been lost to flooding. The root cause is wealthy households' land encroachment and the flight of the poor. Boundaries should first be restored according to precedent, but the matter is so large in scope that it must not be undertaken lightly unless every disposition is thoroughly sound."

sentences.zh: 」書累數萬言，切中其弊。

translations.literal: The memorial totaled tens of thousands of words and struck to the heart of the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran to tens of thousands of words and struck at the heart of the abuses.

sentences.zh: 俄拜監察御史，首言御史有封事，宜專達聖聰，不宜臺臣先有所可否。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Censor and first stated that when censors have sealed memorials, they should reach the sacred ear exclusively and that censorate members should not first express approval or disapproval.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed surveillance censor and argued first of all that sealed memorials from censors should reach the emperor directly, without prior approval or rejection by other censorate members.

sentences.zh: 陞臺都事，遷山北廉訪副使，復召為工部郎中，言考工一十九事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censorate secretariat supervisor, transferred to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Shanbei Commission, and again summoned as Director of the Ministry of Works, where he presented nineteen matters on the examination of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censorate secretariat supervisor, transferred to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Commission, and again summoned as director of the Ministry of Works, where he presented nineteen proposals on public works.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，河決白茅堤，又決金堤，並河郡邑，民居昏墊，壯者流離。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng the Yellow River burst the Baimao embankment and also burst the Jin embankment; prefectures and counties along the river had dwellings drowned in darkness and mire, and the able-bodied fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: In 1344 the Yellow River burst the Baimao embankment and then the Jin embankment; towns along the river were inundated and the able-bodied fled as refugees.

sentences.zh: 帝甚患之，遣使體驗，仍督大臣訪求治河方略，特命魯行都水監。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly troubled, dispatched envoys to investigate on the spot, and still urged the great ministers to seek strategies for controlling the river; Lu was specially ordered to act as Director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled, dispatched envoys to inspect the damage, and urged his ministers to seek a strategy for controlling the river; Lu was specially ordered to serve as acting director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 魯循行河道，考察地形，往復數千里，備得要害，為圖上進二策：其一，議修築北堤，以制橫潰，則用工省；

translations.literal: Lu traveled along the river course, examined the terrain, went back and forth several thousand li, grasped the vital points in full, and submitted a map with two strategies: the first proposed building the northern embankment to control lateral breaches, which would economize on labor;
translations.idiomatic: Lu traveled the river course, surveyed the terrain over thousands of li, mastered every critical point, and submitted a map with two strategies: the first proposed building the northern embankment to control lateral breaches, which would require less labor;

sentences.zh: 其一，議疏塞並舉，挽河東行，使復故道，其功數倍。

translations.literal: the second proposed dredging and blocking together, drawing the river eastward to restore the old course, with labor several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: the second proposed dredging and blocking together, drawing the river eastward to restore its old course, with labor several times greater.

sentences.zh: 會遷右司郎中，議未及竟。

translations.literal: Just then he was transferred to Director of the Right Secretariat Department, and the deliberation did not reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he was transferred to director of the Right Secretariat Department, and the deliberation was left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 其在右司，言時政二十一事，皆見舉行。

translations.literal: While in the Right Department he spoke on twenty-one matters of current policy, all of which were adopted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Right Department he presented twenty-one proposals on current policy, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 調都漕運使，復以漕事二十事言之，朝廷取其八事：一曰京畿和糴，二曰優恤漕司舊領漕戶，三曰接連委官，四曰通州緫治豫定委官，五曰船戶困於壩夫，海運壞於壩戶，六曰疏濬運河，七曰臨清運糧萬戶府當隸漕司，八曰宣忠船戶付本司節制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Director of the Capital Grain Transport, and again presented twenty matters on transport; the court adopted eight of them: first, equitable purchase in the capital region; second, favorable treatment for transport households formerly under the transport office; third, continuous appointment of officials; fourth, overall governance at Tongzhou with pre-designated appointees; fifth, boat households oppressed by dam laborers and sea transport ruined by dam households; sixth, dredging the Grand Canal; seventh, the Linqing Transport Grain Ten-Thousand-Households Office should be subordinate to the transport office; eighth, the Xuanzhong boat households should be placed under this office's control.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to director of the Capital Grain Transport, he presented twenty proposals on transport affairs; the court adopted eight: equitable grain purchase in the capital region; favorable treatment for transport households formerly under the transport office; continuous appointment of officials; unified governance at Tongzhou with pre-designated appointees; relief for boat households oppressed by dam laborers and for sea transport disrupted by dam households; dredging the Grand Canal; subordinating the Linqing Transport Grain Ten-Thousand-Households Office to the transport directorate; and placing the Xuanzhong boat households under its control.

sentences.zh: 事未盡行。

translations.literal: The matters were not fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Not all of these measures were fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 既而河水北侵安山，淪入運河，延袤濟南、河間，將隳兩漕司鹽場，實妨國計。

translations.literal: Before long the river water invaded Anshan from the north, sank into the Grand Canal, and extended across Jinan and Hejian; it was about to destroy the salt fields of both transport commissions, truly obstructing the national revenue plan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the river invaded Anshan from the north and poured into the Grand Canal, spreading across Jinan and Hejian and threatening to destroy the salt fields of both transport commissions—a serious blow to state revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，太傅、右丞相脫脫復相，論及河決，思拯民艱，以塞詔旨，乃集廷臣群議，言人人殊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to office; discussing the river breach, he thought to relieve the people's hardship and satisfy the imperial edict, and therefore assembled the court ministers for collective deliberation, but each man's words differed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to office. Discussing the river breach, he wished to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, and convened the court for deliberation—but opinions diverged widely.

sentences.zh: 魯昌言：「河必當治。

translations.literal: Lu spoke forthrightly: "The river must be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: Lu spoke forthrightly: "The river must be brought under control."

sentences.zh: 」復以前二策進，丞相取其後策，與魯定議，且以其事屬魯。

translations.literal: He again advanced the previous two strategies; the chancellor took the latter strategy, settled the plan with Lu, and entrusted the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: He again presented his two earlier strategies; the chancellor chose the second, settled the plan with Lu, and entrusted the entire project to him.

sentences.zh: 魯固辭，丞相曰：「此事非子不可。

translations.literal: Lu firmly declined, and the chancellor said: "This matter cannot be done without you."
translations.idiomatic: Lu firmly declined, but the chancellor said: "This cannot be done without you."

sentences.zh: 」乃入奏，大稱帝旨。

translations.literal: He then entered to memorialize, and it greatly accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu then memorialized the throne, and the proposal met with the emperor's full approval.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，命魯以工部尚書、緫治河防使，進秩二品，授以銀章，領河南、北諸路軍民，發汴梁、大名十有三路民一十五萬，廬州等戍十有八翼軍二萬供役，一切從事大小軍民官，咸稟節度，便宜興繕。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Lu was ordered, as Minister of Works and Commissioner-General for River Control, to advance to second rank, was granted a silver seal, and put in charge of military and civilian personnel of all circuits south and north of the Yellow River; one hundred fifty thousand civilians from thirteen circuits including Bianliang and Daming and twenty thousand troops from eighteen garrison wings including Luzhou were mobilized for labor; all participating officials, great and small, military and civilian, were subject to his command, with discretionary authority to undertake construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1351 Lu was appointed minister of works and commissioner-general for river control, promoted to second rank and granted a silver seal. He was put in charge of military and civilian personnel across all circuits north and south of the Yellow River, with 150,000 civilians from thirteen circuits including Bianliang and Daming and 20,000 troops from eighteen garrison wings mobilized for labor. All participating officials were placed under his command with discretionary authority to undertake construction.

sentences.zh: 是月鳩工，七月鑿河成，八月決水故河，九月舟楫通，十一月諸埽諸堤成，水土工畢，河復故道。

translations.literal: That month labor was assembled; in the seventh month the river channel was cut through; in the eighth month water was released into the old course; in the ninth month boats and oars passed; in the eleventh month all revetments and embankments were completed, earth and water works finished, and the river restored its old course.
translations.idiomatic: That month work began; by the seventh month the new channel was cut; in the eighth month water was released into the old course; by the ninth month boats could pass; by the eleventh month all revetments and embankments were complete. Earth and water works finished, the river had returned to its old course.

sentences.zh: 事見河渠志。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使報祭河伯，召魯還京師，魯以河平圖獻。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to report the sacrifice to the River Lord and summoned Lu back to the capital; Lu presented a map of the pacified river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched envoys to report the sacrifice to the River Lord and summoned Lu back to the capital, where Lu presented a map of the pacified river.

sentences.zh: 帝適覽臺臣奏疏，請褒脫脫治河之績，次論魯功，超拜榮祿大夫、集賢大學士，賞賚金帛，敕翰林丞旨歐陽玄製河平碑，以旌脫脫勞績，具載魯功，且宣付史館，并贈魯先臣三世。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then reading censorate memorials requesting commendation for Toghto's achievements in controlling the river; next they discussed Lu's merit. He was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Academician-Exceller of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks; the Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts Ouyang Xuan was ordered to compose a stele on the pacified river to honor Toghto's labor and record Lu's achievements in full, and to have it proclaimed and sent to the History Office; Lu's ancestors for three generations were also enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just then reading censorate memorials praising Toghto's achievements in controlling the river and commending Lu's contribution. Lu was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing and Academician-Exceller of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and rewarded with gold and silks. Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts Ouyang Xuan was ordered to compose a stele commemorating the pacified river, honoring Toghto's labor while recording Lu's achievements in full; the text was proclaimed and sent to the History Office, and Lu's ancestors for three generations were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書左丞，從脫脫平徐州，脫脫既旋師，命魯追餘黨，分攻濠州，同緫兵官平章月可察兒督戰，魯誓師曰：「吾奉旨統八衛漢軍，頓兵于濠七日矣。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Secretariat and followed Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou; after Toghto withdrew his army, Lu was ordered to pursue the remnant band, divide forces to attack Haozhou, and together with the commander-in-chief, Grand Councillor Yuekechuer, supervise the campaign. Lu addressed the army in oath, saying: "I have received orders to command the Han armies of eight guards and have encamped at Haozhou for seven days already.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed left chancellor of the Secretariat and accompanied Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou. After Toghto withdrew, Lu was ordered to pursue the remnant rebels and attack Haozhou, with Grand Councillor Yuekechuer as commander-in-chief. Addressing the troops, Lu swore: "By imperial order I command the Han armies of eight guards and have been encamped at Haozhou for seven days.

sentences.zh: 爾諸將同心協力，必以今日巳、午時取城池，然後食。

translations.literal: You generals must unite hearts and combine strength; you must take the city between the si and wu hours today, and only then eat."
translations.idiomatic: You generals must unite and fight as one—you must take the city between the fifth and seventh hours today, and only then eat."

sentences.zh: 」魯上馬麾進，抵城下，忽頭眩下馬，且戒兵馬弗散，病愈亟，却藥不肯汗，竟卒于軍中，年五十七。

translations.literal: Lu mounted his horse and waved the advance; reaching below the wall he suddenly felt dizzy and dismounted, yet warned the troops not to disperse; his illness grew acute with extreme speed; he refused medicine and would not sweat, and in the end died in the army at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Lu mounted and led the charge; reaching the wall he suddenly grew dizzy and dismounted, yet ordered the troops not to disperse. His illness worsened with terrifying speed; he refused medicine and would not sweat, and died in camp at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月壬午也。

translations.literal: This was on the renwu day of the fifth month of the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the renwu day of the fifth month of 1353.

sentences.zh: 月可察兒躬為治喪，選士護柩還高平，有旨賜交鈔五百錠以給葬事。

translations.literal: Yuekechuer personally arranged the funeral, selected men to escort the coffin back to Gaoping, and an edict granted five hundred ingots of paper money for burial expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuekechuer personally arranged the funeral, selected men to escort the coffin back to Gaoping, and an edict granted five hundred ingots of paper money for burial expenses.

sentences.zh: 子稹。

translations.literal: His son was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 逯魯曾

translations.literal: Lu Luceng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luceng

sentences.zh: 逯魯曾字善止，修武人。

translations.literal: Lu Luceng, courtesy name Shanzhi, was a native of Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luceng, styled Shanzhi, was a native of Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 性剛介，通經術，中天曆二年進士第，授翰林國史院編修官，辟御史臺掾，掌機密。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upright, versed in the classics and their arts; in the second year of Tianshun he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Compiler of the Hanlin National History Academy, was recruited as a Censorate clerk, and managed confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and upright and well versed in the classics. In 1329 he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed compiler of the Hanlin National History Academy, recruited as a censorate clerk, and entrusted with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劾中丞史顯夫簡傲，魯曾開實封於大夫前曰：「中丞素持重，不能與人周旋，御史以人情劾之，非公論。

translations.literal: A surveillance censor impeached the Censor-in-Chief Shi Xianfu for arrogance and aloofness. Luceng opened the sealed memorial before the great ministers and said: "The Censor-in-Chief has always been grave and weighty and cannot engage in social maneuvering; the censor impeaches him on personal grounds—this is not public judgment."
translations.idiomatic: When a surveillance censor impeached Censor-in-Chief Shi Xianfu for arrogance, Luceng opened the sealed memorial before the assembled ministers and said: "The censor-in-chief has always been grave and reserved and is not skilled at social maneuvering. To impeach him on personal grounds is not impartial judgment."

sentences.zh: 」由是皆知其直。

translations.literal: " From this all knew his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From this everyone knew his integrity.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 武宗一廟，未立后主配享，集群臣廷議之。

translations.literal: For Emperor Wuzong's single temple, no principal consort had been established for joint sacrifice; the ministers were assembled for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Wuzong's temple no principal consort had yet been designated for joint sacrifice, and the ministers were summoned to deliberate at court.

sentences.zh: 魯曾抗言：「先朝以武宗皇后真哥無子，不立其主。

translations.literal: Luceng spoke forthrightly: "The previous court, because Empress Zhenge of Wuzong had no son, did not establish her as principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: Luceng spoke forthrightly: "The previous court, because Empress Zhenge of Wuzong had no son, did not install her as principal consort.

sentences.zh: 」時伯顏為右丞相，以為明宗之母亦乞列氏，可以配享。

translations.literal: " At that time Bayan was Right Chancellor and held that the mother of Emperor Mingzong, also of the Qigilie clan, could serve in joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bayan was right chancellor and argued that Emperor Mingzong's mother, also of the Qigilie clan, could be installed for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 徽政院傳太后旨，以文宗之母唐兀氏可以配享。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Palace Governance transmitted the Empress Dowager's order that the mother of Emperor Wenzong, of the Tangut clan, could serve in joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Palace Governance transmitted the empress dowager's order that Emperor Wenzong's mother, of the Tangut clan, could be installed for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 伯顏問魯曾曰：「先朝既以真哥皇后無子，不為立主，今所立者，明宗母乎？

translations.literal: Bayan asked Luceng: "Since the previous court, because Empress Zhenge had no son, did not establish a principal consort, whom should be established now—the mother of Mingzong?
translations.idiomatic: Bayan asked Luceng: "Since the previous court did not install a principal consort because Empress Zhenge had no son, whom should we install now—Mingzong's mother?

sentences.zh: 文宗母乎？

translations.literal: Or the mother of Wenzong?"
translations.idiomatic: Or Wenzong's mother?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「真哥皇后在武宗朝，已膺玉冊，則為武宗皇后，明宗、文宗二母后，固為妾也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Empress Zhenge in the Wuzong reign had already received the jade book; she was thus Empress of Wuzong, while the two mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Empress Zhenge had already received the jade book in the Wuzong reign and was thus Wuzong's empress, while the mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong were by status concubines.

sentences.zh: 今以無子之故，不為立主，以妾后為正宮，是為臣而廢先君之后，為子而追封先父之妾，於禮不可。

translations.literal: Now, on the grounds of having no son, not establishing a principal consort but making a concubine empress the principal palace—this is, as a subject, abolishing the empress of the former lord, and, as a son, posthumously ennobling the concubine of the former father; in ritual it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse a principal consort because she had no son, yet elevate a concubine to the principal palace, is for a subject to displace a former sovereign's empress and for a son to ennoble his father's concubine posthumously—this is impermissible by ritual.

sentences.zh: 且燕王垂即位，追廢其母后，而立其生母為后，以配享先王，為萬世笑，豈可復蹈其失乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, when Prince of Yan Chui took the throne, he posthumously deposed his mother's empress status and established his birth mother as empress for joint sacrifice with the former king—a laughingstock for ten thousand generations; how can we tread that error again?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Prince of Yan, Murong Chui, took the throne he deposed his mother's empress status and installed his birth mother as empress for joint sacrifice—a laughingstock for all ages. How can we repeat that error?

sentences.zh: 」集賢大學士陳顥，素嫉魯曾，出曰：「唐太宗冊曹王明之母為后，是亦二后也，豈不可乎？

translations.literal: " Academician-Exceller of the Hall of Gathered Worthies Chen Hao, who had long resented Luceng, came forward and said: "Emperor Taizong of Tang enfeoffed the mother of Prince of Cao Li Ming as empress—there were also two empresses; how can it not be permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: Academician-Exceller Chen Hao, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang ennobled the mother of Prince of Cao Li Ming as empress—there were two empresses then as well. Why should it not be permissible?"

sentences.zh: 」魯曾曰：「堯之母為帝嚳庶妃，堯立為帝，未聞冊以為后而配嚳。

translations.literal: Luceng said: "Yao's mother was a secondary consort of Emperor Ku; when Yao was established as emperor, one never heard of her being enfeoffed as empress to share sacrifice with Ku.
translations.idiomatic: Luceng replied: "Yao's mother was a secondary consort of Emperor Ku; when Yao became emperor, we never hear of her being enfeoffed as empress to share sacrifice with Ku.

sentences.zh: 皇上為大元天子，不法堯、舜，而法唐太宗邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven of the Great Yuan; will you not take Yao and Shun as law but take Emperor Taizong of Tang as law?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven of the Great Yuan—will you not take Yao and Shun as your model but emulate Emperor Taizong of Tang?"

sentences.zh: 」衆服其議，而伯顏韙之，遂以真哥皇后配焉。

translations.literal: The assembly was convinced by his argument, and Bayan approved it; Empress Zhenge was thereupon installed for joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was persuaded by his argument, Bayan approved, and Empress Zhenge was installed for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 復拜監察御史，劾荅失海牙、阿吉剌太尉，鞏卜班右丞，兀突蠻刑部尚書，吉當普監察御史，哈剌完者、月魯不花院使，呂思誠郎中，皆黜之。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Surveillance Censor and impeached Dashihaiya and Aijila, Grand Marshals; Gongbuban, Right Chancellor; Utuman, Minister of Punishments; Jidangpu, Surveillance Censor; Haragwanser and Yuelubuhua, Bureau Commissioners; and Lü Sicheng, Director—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Again appointed surveillance censor, he impeached Dashihaiya and Aijila, grand marshals; Gongbuban, right chancellor; Utuman, minister of punishments; Jidangpu, surveillance censor; Haragwanser and Yuelubuhua, bureau commissioners; and Lü Sicheng, director—all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 八人之中，惟思誠少過，亦變祖宗選法，餘皆伯顏之黨，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: Among the eight men, only Sicheng had minor faults, yet even he had altered the ancestral selection law; the rest were all Bayan's faction, and the court was awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: Of the eight, only Sicheng had minor faults, yet even he had altered the ancestral selection law; the rest were Bayan's faction, and the court was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 除樞密院都事，上言：「前伯顏專殺大臣，其黨利其妻女，巧誣以罪。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretariat supervisor of the Bureau of Military Affairs and submitted a memorial: "Formerly Bayan arbitrarily executed great ministers; his faction coveted their wives and daughters and craftily framed them with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed secretariat supervisor of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he memorialized: "Formerly Bayan arbitrarily executed great ministers; his faction coveted their wives and daughters and craftily framed them with crimes.

sentences.zh: 今大小官及諸人有罪，止坐其身，不得籍其妻女。

translations.literal: Now when officials great and small and all other persons are guilty, only they themselves should be punished; their wives and daughters must not be registered for confiscation."
translations.idiomatic: Now when officials or private persons are guilty, only the offender himself should be punished; their wives and daughters must not be registered for confiscation."

sentences.zh: 郯王為伯顏搆陷，妻女流離，當雪其無辜，給復子孫。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tan was framed by Bayan; his wife and daughters were scattered in exile; their innocence should be cleared and their descendants restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tan was framed by Bayan; his wife and daughters were scattered in exile. Their innocence should be cleared and their descendants restored to status.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 除刑部員外郎，悉辨正橫罹伯顏所誣者。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Punishments and fully rectified those who had been falsely implicated by Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, he fully rectified those falsely implicated by Bayan.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正府郎中，出為遼陽行省左右司郎中，除僉山北道肅政廉訪司事，入為禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, went out as Director of the Left and Right Secretariat Departments of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, was appointed Associate Surveillance Commissioner of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission, and entered as Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, served as director of the Left and Right Secretariat Departments of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, was appointed associate surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission, and entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，丞相脫脫討徐州賊，以官軍不習水土，募瀕海鹽丁為軍，乃超遷魯曾資善大夫、淮南宣慰使，領征討事，遣其募鹽丁五千人從征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels; because the government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and sent to recruit five thousand salt workers to follow the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and sent to recruit five thousand salt workers for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 徐州平，繼使領所部軍討淮東，卒於軍。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, he was next dispatched to lead his troops in campaigning against Huaidong and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuzhou was pacified he was dispatched to lead his troops against Huaidong and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 貢師泰

translations.literal: Gong Shitai
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shitai

sentences.zh: 貢師泰字泰甫，寧國之宣城人。

translations.literal: Gong Shitai, courtesy name Taifu, was a native of Xuancheng in Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shitai, styled Taifu, was a native of Xuancheng in Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 父奎，以文學名家，延祐、至治間，官京師，為集賢直學士，卒，諡文靖。

translations.literal: His father Kui was renowned for literary learning; between the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he served in the capital as Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, died, and was posthumously titled Duke of Culture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui was renowned for literary learning; during the Yanyou and Zhizhi reigns he served in the capital as academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, died, and was posthumously titled Duke of Culture.

sentences.zh: 師泰早肄業國子學為諸生。

translations.literal: Shitai early studied at the Imperial Academy as a student.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai studied early at the Imperial Academy as a student.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，釋褐出身，授從仕郎、太和州判官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he left student robes and entered office, appointed Gentleman for Attendance and Assistant Prefect of Taihe Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1327 he left student robes for office, appointed gentleman for attendance and assistant prefect of Taihe Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，改徽州路歙縣丞，江浙行省辟為掾，尋以土著，自劾去。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father, was changed to Assistant Magistrate of She County in Huizhou Circuit, was recruited as a clerk by the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, but soon because he was a native of the place impeached himself and left.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was appointed assistant magistrate of She County in Huizhou Circuit and recruited as a clerk by the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, but soon resigned on the ground that as a native of the region he should not hold the post.

sentences.zh: 大臣有以其名聞者，擢應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: A great minister had his name brought to notice, and he was promoted to Attendant Drafter of Hanlin Documents.
translations.idiomatic: When a great minister brought his name to the court's attention, he was promoted to attendant drafter of Hanlin documents.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服闋，除紹興路緫管府推官，郡有疑獄，悉為詳讞而剖決之。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Judicial Investigator of the Shaoxing Circuit General Administration, and in doubtful cases in the prefecture he fully reviewed the verdicts and decided them.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he was appointed judicial investigator of the Shaoxing Circuit General Administration; in every doubtful case in the prefecture he reviewed the verdicts in detail and rendered judgment.

sentences.zh: 山陰白洋港有大船飄近岸，史甲二十人，適取鹵海濱，見其無主，因取其篙櫓，而船中有二死人。

translations.literal: At Baiyang Harbor in Shanyin a large ship drifted near shore; twenty men surnamed Shi happened to be gathering brine by the sea, saw that it had no owner, and therefore took its poles and oars, but in the ship were two dead men.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiyang Harbor in Shanyin a large ship drifted ashore. Twenty men surnamed Shi, who happened to be gathering brine by the sea, saw no owner aboard and took its poles and oars—but the ship held two dead men.

sentences.zh: 有徐乙者，怪其無物而有死人，稱為史等所劫。

translations.literal: A man named Xu Yi found it strange that there were no goods but there were dead men, and declared that Shi and the others had robbed the ship.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xu Yi found it strange that the ship held no goods but two corpses, and accused Shi and the others of robbery and murder.

sentences.zh: 史傭作富民高丙家，事遂連高。

translations.literal: Shi was hired labor in the household of the wealthy man Gao Bing, and the case thus implicated Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was hired labor in the household of the wealthy man Gao Bing, and the case thus implicated Gao as well.

sentences.zh: 史既誣服，高亦就逮。

translations.literal: Shi had already confessed under false accusation, and Gao was also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had already confessed under coercion, and Gao was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 師泰密詢之，則里中沈丁載物抵杭而回，漁者張網海中，因盜網中魚，為漁者所殺，史實未嘗殺人奪物，高亦弗知情，其冤皆白。

translations.literal: Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, had been netting fish at sea; because he stole fish from another's net he was killed by the fisherman. Shi had in fact never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao also did not know; their wrongful convictions were all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that Shen Ding of the village, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, had been fishing at sea; he stole fish from another's net and was killed by the fisherman. Shi had never killed or robbed anyone, and Gao knew nothing of the matter—their wrongful convictions were all cleared.

sentences.zh: 游徼徐裕，以巡鹽為名，肆暴村落間。

translations.literal: The patrol officer Xu Yu, under the name of inspecting salt, committed violence wantonly among the villages.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol officer Xu Yu, under the pretext of inspecting salt, committed violence wantonly in the villages.

sentences.zh: 一日，遇諸暨商，奪其所齎錢，撲殺之，投尸於水，走告縣曰：「我獲私鹽犯人，畏罪赴水死矣。

translations.literal: One day he encountered a merchant from Zhuji, seized the money he carried, beat him to death, threw the corpse into the water, and ran to report to the county: "I captured a private-salt offender who, fearing punishment, threw himself into the water and died."
translations.idiomatic: One day he met a merchant from Zhuji, seized his money, beat him to death, threw the body into the water, and reported to the county: "I captured a private-salt offender who, fearing punishment, drowned himself."

sentences.zh: 」官驗視，以有傷，疑之。

translations.literal: Officials examined the body and, finding wounds, were suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Officials examined the body, found wounds, and grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 遂以疑獄釋。

translations.literal: The case was therefore released as doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: The case was therefore left unresolved as doubtful.

sentences.zh: 師泰追詢覆按之，具得裕所以殺人狀，復俾待報。

translations.literal: Shitai pursued inquiries and re-examined the case, fully obtaining the circumstances of Yu's murder, and had him held awaiting sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai pursued inquiries and re-examined the case, fully establishing how Yu had committed murder, and had him held awaiting sentence.

sentences.zh: 餘姚孫國賓，以求盜，獲姚甲造偽鈔，受賕而釋之，執高乙、魯丙赴有司，誣以同造偽。

translations.literal: Sun Guobin of Yuyao, in pursuit of thieves, captured Yao Jia counterfeiting paper money, accepted a bribe and released him, then seized Gao Yi and Lu Bing and brought them to the authorities, falsely accusing them of joint counterfeiting.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guobin of Yuyao, while pursuing thieves, captured Yao Jia counterfeiting paper money, accepted a bribe and released him, then seized Gao Yi and Lu Bing and brought them to the authorities on false charges of joint counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 高嘗為姚行用，實非自造，孫既舍姚，因加罪於高，而魯與孫有隙，故并連之，魯與高未嘗相識也。

translations.literal: Gao had once circulated Yao's notes but had not himself counterfeited; since Sun had already released Yao, he therefore added guilt to Gao, and because Lu had a grudge with Sun he was also implicated—Lu and Gao had never known each other.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had once circulated Yao's notes but had not counterfeited them himself; since Sun had already released Yao, he shifted the blame onto Gao. Because Lu had a grudge against Sun, he was implicated as well—though Lu and Gao had never even met.

sentences.zh: 師泰疑高等覆造不合，以孫詰之，辭屈而情見。

translations.literal: Shitai doubted that Gao and the others had repeatedly counterfeited and that this did not fit; he interrogated Sun, whose words were defeated and the truth appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai doubted that Gao and the others could have repeatedly counterfeited as charged; he interrogated Sun, whose testimony collapsed and the truth emerged.

sentences.zh: 即釋魯而加高以本罪，姚遂處死，孫亦就法。

translations.literal: He immediately released Lu and imposed on Gao his proper offense; Yao was then executed, and Sun also suffered the law.
translations.idiomatic: He released Lu immediately and imposed on Gao only his proper offense; Yao was executed, and Sun was punished by law as well.

sentences.zh: 其於冤獄詳讞之明多類此。

translations.literal: His clarity in detailed verdicts on wrongful cases was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His clarity in reviewing wrongful convictions was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 以故郡民自以不冤，治行為諸郡第一。

translations.literal: For this reason the people of the prefecture considered themselves free from injustice, and his administrative record ranked first among all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the people of the prefecture felt they were treated justly, and his administrative record ranked first among all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 考滿，復入翰林為應奉，預修后妃、功臣列傳，事畢，遷宣文閣授經郎，歷翰林待制、國子司業，擢禮部郎中，再遷吏部，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When his term evaluation was complete he re-entered the Hanlin as Attendant Drafter, participated in compiling the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers; when the work was finished he was transferred to Lecturer of the Hall of Propagating Culture, served as Hanlin Attendant Drafter and Vice Director of the Imperial Academy, was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites, was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and was appointed Surveillance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was complete he returned to the Hanlin as attendant drafter and participated in compiling the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers. When the work was finished he was transferred to lecturer of the Hall of Propagating Culture, served as Hanlin attendant drafter and vice director of the Imperial Academy, was promoted to director of the Ministry of Rites, transferred again to the Ministry of Personnel, and appointed surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 自世祖以後，省臺之職，南人斥不用，及是，始復舊制，於是南士復得居省臺，自師泰始，時論以為得人。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shizu, southerners had been rejected from Secretariat and Censorate posts; only now was the old system restored, and southerners could again hold Secretariat and Censorate offices—beginning with Shitai, whom contemporary opinion held to be the right man for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Shizu southerners had been barred from Secretariat and Censorate posts; only now was the old system restored, and southerners could again serve in those offices—beginning with Shitai, whom contemporaries hailed as the right appointment.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng he was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時江淮兵起，京師食不足，師泰奉命和糴于浙右，得糧百萬石，以給京師。

translations.literal: At that time warfare arose in the Jiang-Huai region and the capital lacked food; Shitai received orders to purchase grain equitably in western Zhejiang, obtained one million piculs of grain, and supplied the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare had broken out in the Jiang-Huai region and the capital lacked food. Shitai was ordered to purchase grain equitably in western Zhejiang, obtained one million piculs, and supplied the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以京師至上都，驛戶凋弊，命師泰巡視整飭之。

translations.literal: The court, because the courier households between the capital and Shangdu were depleted and ruined, ordered Shitai to inspect and rectify them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the courier households along the route from the capital to Shangdu were depleted and ruined, the court ordered Shitai to inspect and rectify them.

sentences.zh: 至則歷究其病原，驗其富貧，而均其徭役，數十郡之民，賴以稍蘇。

translations.literal: On arrival he thoroughly investigated the root causes of disease, verified wealth and poverty, and equalized corvée labor; the people of dozens of prefectures relied on this for slight recovery.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he thoroughly investigated the root causes of their distress, assessed wealth and poverty, and equalized corvée burdens; the people of dozens of prefectures were somewhat relieved.

sentences.zh: 豪貴以其不利於己，深嫉之，然莫能有所中傷也。

translations.literal: Powerful families, because this was not to their advantage, deeply resented him, yet could not harm him in any way.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families deeply resented him because the reforms harmed their interests, yet could not find any way to injure him.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷欲仍和糴浙西，因除師泰都水庸田使。

translations.literal: When the court wished again to purchase grain equitably in western Zhejiang, Shitai was therefore appointed Commissioner of Water Control and Abandoned Fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished again to purchase grain equitably in western Zhejiang, Shitai was appointed commissioner of water control and abandoned fields.

sentences.zh: 十五年，庸田司罷，擢江西廉訪副使，未行，遷福建廉訪使，居亡何，除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Abandoned Fields Office was abolished; he was promoted to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi but did not depart, was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, and after a short time was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1355 the Abandoned Fields Office was abolished; he was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi but did not depart, was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Fujian, and shortly afterward was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時平江缺守，廷議難其人，師泰又以選為平江路緫管。

translations.literal: At that time Pingjiang lacked a prefect; court deliberation found no suitable man, and Shitai was again selected as General Manager of Pingjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang then lacked a prefect; the court could find no suitable candidate, and Shitai was again selected as general manager of Pingjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，甫視事，張士誠自高郵率衆渡江，直抵城下，攻圍甚急。

translations.literal: That winter, just as he took office, Zhang Shicheng led his forces from Gaoyou across the river, advanced straight to below the city wall, and besieged it with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, just as he took office, Zhang Shicheng led his forces from Gaoyou across the Yangtze, advanced straight to the city walls, and laid siege with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 明年春，守將弗能支，斬關遁去，師泰領義兵出戰，力不敵，亦懷印綬棄城遁，匿海濱者久之。

translations.literal: The next spring the defending general could not hold out, cut through the gate and fled; Shitai led militia out to fight, was no match in strength, also took his seal and sash and abandoned the city in flight, hiding by the seashore for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the defending general could not hold out, cut through the gate and fled. Shitai led militia out to fight but was overpowered; he too took his seal and sash, abandoned the city, and hid by the seashore for a long time.

sentences.zh: 士誠既納降，江浙行省丞相達識帖睦邇，以便宜授師泰兩浙都轉運鹽使。

translations.literal: After Shicheng had submitted, Toghuz Temür, Chancellor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, by discretionary authority appointed Shitai Director of the Two-Zhe Salt Transport.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shicheng submitted, Toghuz Temür, chancellor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, by discretionary authority appointed Shitai director of the Two-Zhe Salt Transport.

sentences.zh: 至則剔其積蠹，通其利源，大課以集，國用資之。

translations.literal: On arrival he eliminated accumulated corruption, opened sources of profit, and great revenue was gathered; state finances relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he eliminated accumulated corruption, opened sources of revenue, and great tax yields were gathered, on which state finances relied.

sentences.zh: 丞相復承制除師泰江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: The chancellor again, by imperial commission, appointed Shitai Associate Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor again, by imperial commission, appointed Shitai associate administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，朝廷除戶部尚書，俾分部閩中，以閩鹽易糧，由海道轉運給京師，凡為糧數十萬石，朝廷賴焉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the court appointed him Minister of Revenue and ordered him to branch-office in Fujian, exchanging Fujian salt for grain and transporting it by sea route to supply the capital; in all several hundred thousand piculs of grain were provided, on which the court relied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1360 the court appointed him minister of revenue and ordered him to branch-office in Fujian, exchanging Fujian salt for grain and transporting it by sea to supply the capital—several hundred thousand piculs in all, on which the court relied.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，召為祕書卿，行至杭之海寧，得疾而卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was summoned as Secretary of the Palace Library; traveling to Haining in Hangzhou, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1362 he was summoned as secretary of the Palace Library; traveling to Haining near Hangzhou, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 師泰性倜儻，狀貌偉然，既以文字知名，而於政事尤長，所至績效輒暴著。

translations.literal: Shitai was by nature free and unrestrained, of imposing appearance; already renowned for literary composition, he was especially skilled in government affairs, and wherever he went his achievements were conspicuously displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai was free-spirited and imposing in appearance; already renowned for his writing, he was especially skilled in government, and wherever he served his achievements were conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 尤喜接引後進，士之賢，不問識不識，即加推轂，以故士譽翕然咸歸之。

translations.literal: He especially delighted in guiding and advancing the younger generation; for worthy scholars, whether he knew them or not, he immediately gave a push at the wheel, and for this reason scholarly praise converged upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He especially delighted in mentoring younger scholars; for any worthy man, whether he knew him or not, he would give his full support, and for this reason scholarly praise converged upon him.

sentences.zh: 有詩文若干卷行于世。

translations.literal: He had poetry and prose in several juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose, totaling several juan, circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 周伯琦

translations.literal: Zhou Boqi
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Boqi

sentences.zh: 周伯琦字伯溫，饒州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Boqi, courtesy name Bowen, was a native of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Boqi, styled Bowen, was a native of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 父應極，至大間，仁宗為皇太子，召見，獻皇元頌，為言于武宗，以為翰林待制。

translations.literal: His father Yingji, during the Zhide period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned for audience, presented an ode on the founding of the Yuan, spoke on his behalf to Wuzong, and was made Hanlin Attendant Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingji, during the Zhide period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned to audience, presented an ode on the founding of the Yuan, spoke on his behalf to Wuzong, and was made Hanlin attendant drafter.

sentences.zh: 後為皇太子說書，日侍英邸。

translations.literal: Later he was lecturer to the crown prince and daily attended the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as lecturer to the crown prince and attended the princely residence daily.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷集賢待制，終池州路同知緫管府事。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant Drafter of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and ended as Associate Manager of the Chizhou Circuit General Administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne he was transferred to Hanlin attendant drafter of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and ended his career as associate manager of the Chizhou Circuit General Administration.

sentences.zh: 伯琦自幼從宦，游京師，入國學，為上舍生，積分及高等。

translations.literal: Boqi from youth followed his father's official career, traveled to the capital, entered the Imperial Academy as an upper-hall student, and accumulated credits to the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: Boqi from youth followed his father's official career, traveled to the capital, entered the Imperial Academy as an upper-hall student, and accumulated credits to the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 去，以蔭授將仕郎、南海縣主簿，三轉為翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He left, received a yin appointment as Gentleman for Service and Registrar of Nanhai County, and after three transfers became Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He left the academy, received a yin appointment as gentleman for service and registrar of Nanhai County, and after three promotions became Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，改奎章閣為宣文閣、藝文監為崇文監，伯琦為宣文閣授經郎，教戚里大臣子弟，每進講，輒稱旨，且日被顧問。
